contexts.text: The seed of a homer shall yield an ephah () = that there are so few remains of celestial things.
A homer is predicated of good, because it is a measure of wheat and barley; in like manner an ephah.
An ehpah = good... because by it and the homer dry things were measured which served as food; as wheat, barley, fine flour... Illustrated.
That an ephah = good is evident from the places where the meat-offering is treated of, for which the meal of fine flour was measured by the ephah. Illustrated. And the meat-offering = good.
A woman in the midst of the ephah () = evil in good.

The ephah and the hin were measures, and by measures is signified the quantity of the thing treated of. By the ephah, which was a measure of fine flour, of wheat, and of barley, is signified the quantity of good; and by a hin, which was a measure of wine and of oil, the quantity of truth. The tenth part of an ephah is what is meant here (). Explained. AC 10262:2.
The ephah was divided into ten parts... in order that it might signify what is receptive... for ten = much, all, and full.
Hence it is evident, that an ephah = the degree of reception...
